engine: Blood Gauge (BG) starts and ends each encounter at 0, capacity3; Spill Control raises capacity6 while known. Once on your own regular turn, a weapon attack that damages a hostile living creature grants1BG. Hemorrhage Slash uses this same trigger, not an additional one. Explicit critical/kill/refund features can add more, but total BG gained is capped2 per round. Self-inflicted damage, allies, summons, helpless captives and repeated damage to a corpse never generate BG. Blood is an encounter resource, not a currency carried into rest.

Dexterity governs weapon attacks; Intelligence governs hemomancy save DC and M. S scales from Crimson Agent class level. A weapon technique includes only its printed attacks, with normal weapon die plus Dexterity (or Strength when that weapon requires it). No free attack is implied by attack-speed wording. Class BG and RP are separate. Once per turn when casting an ordinary spell, optionally spend1BG to prevent1 of that cast's Dissonance gain, minimum0; never reduce RP this way.

Your Bleed is a physical ongoing effect on a living, non-bloodless creature: 1d4 damage at the start of each of its next3 turns, then ends. It is not a new attack and generates no BG or procs. Refresh duration instead of stacking; Blood Echo expressly allows two independent instances, maximum. An Action by the victim or an adjacent creature using a healer's kit ends all your Bleeds on that victim. Apply physical resistance/immunity normally. Track remaining ticks and creator per instance. Allied healing versions from Bloodweaver cost RP and never count as hostile Bleeds for detonation, spreading or generation.

One Blood Mark at a time on a living target with your Bleed, except Phantom Strike, which explicitly may apply the mark without Bleed. It does not add a free Bleed. Marks last5 of your regular turns, expire on encounter end or if the target dies, and never create damage by themselves. Rupture requires the target still within60ft and line of effect; it spends the mark. A mark does not defeat cover, planar boundaries or bloodlessness. Bloodtrail has its own tracking limits.

Veinweaves are self buffs unless their card expressly allows an ally. They require concentration and one may be active. Crimson Harmony is an explicit exception permitting two Veinweaves as one linked concentration burden; a failed concentration check ends both. A non-Veinweave concentration effect replaces the whole group. BG is spent on activation; no upkeep unless printed. Damage-sharing is redirection before mitigation, not extra damage: apply each recipient's own defenses once and never redirect the redirected portion again.

The healing, execution and denial text below deliberately bounds the source's vague percentage/instant-kill claims. HP sacrificed is direct loss, bypasses temporary HP and defenses, cannot be redirected, and cannot reduce the donor below1. Only a willing ally can donate. HP sacrifice is never damage for class triggers. No class feature here restores the dead or removes Wounds.

At level1 learn the core Blood Gauge/Bleed rules automatically. Blood Mark and Veinweaver's Core remain selections; Quickblood can be selected and used without a second unlock tax. Veinweaver's Core improves that foundation as printed. Standard scheduled acquisition applies. Bloodbound Edge is automatic9. At10 choose Bloodweaver, Shadow Operative or Thirstborn; its Final Cut is automatic20. Duplicate Hemostasis names are separate Arch and Bloodweaver IDs.

Capacity clarification: Blood Gauge automatically reaches capacity6 at class9. Spill Control allows reaching6 early but never raises the cap above6. This new explicit gate ensures a later5-BG Final Cut can be used without an optional capacity selection. Gain cap2/round and encounter reset0 still apply.
workedExample: Bard-style example becomes Agent5: DEX16, INT14, S2, M2, BG0/cap3, full class RP. Select Hemorrhage Slash, Quickblood, Blood Mark, Shroud at1; Blood Tithe and Vital Targeting at2; Rupture and Spill Control at3. Capacity is now6.
Turn1: Hemorrhage Slash hits for ordinary weapon damage+2d6, applies Bleed, and gains1BG (not2). Bonus Action Blood Mark pays1BG: balance0. Target takes its first1d4 Bleed on its next turn.
Turn2: ordinary weapon attack hits and gains1BG. Keep the mark and save resources; Bleed ticks independently and grants no BG.
Turn3: a second weapon hit gains1BG: balance2. Bonus Action Quickblood spends1BG: balance1. It gives movement, not another attack.

Turn4: Rupture is an Action, pays1BG: balance0 and consumes the mark. Target fails CON: takes(S+1)d8=3d8. Rupture is not a weapon hit, so it generates no replacement BG. Any remaining Bleed continues.
After the encounter BG becomes0. Blood Tithe's used short-rest charge and spent RP do not refresh without an actual rest.
balanceQuestions: Does early setup take too many turns for one mark?
Can Bloodweaver protect without sacrifice loops or infinite healing?
Are denial and execution limits sufficient against bosses and multiclass dips?
